P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: Yes, freely. Botswana removed all exchange controls on current-account transactions (IMF Article VIII) and abolished its remaining exchange controls, including capital-account controls, by 1999. No surrender or repatriation rule applies.

P1_fx_receipts.notes: Abolition date 9 Feb 1999 per search summary of the Daily News article (not in the captured quote). AML/KYC rules still apply at banks.

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: Income tax on foreign-source income for residents; rates or special regimes
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: Botswana taxes on a source basis: a resident is taxable on all income from a Botswana source, at progressive rates up to 25% (0% up to BWP 48,000). Whether fees for remote work done in Botswana for foreign clients are Botswana-source (likely, as the work is done there) was not confirmed. Deloitte 2026 confirms the source-based system and the 0% band up to BWP 48,000, rising to 25%.

L5_data_protection.question: Data-protection law applicable to a small online business
L5_data_protection.answer: The Data Protection Act No. 18 of 2024 came into effect on 29 Oct 2024, replacing the never-commenced 2018 Act. The Information and Data Protection Commission keeps a public register of data controllers. Controllers must notify the Commissioner before automated processing, including any proposed transfers to third countries.

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here; Wise does not let residents hold money. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts), Polar, Dodo Payments. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (4) Client payments by PayPal (on PayPal's Payouts list as 'Send, receive, and withdraw'). (5) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
